title: Refused a Clerk's Job, Eli Lilly Opened a Laboratory on Pearl Street
conflicts: First-year sales: Indiana Historical Society gives $3,477 for the first eight months (and $11,318.73 by end-1877); Wikipedia gives $4,470 for 1876. The story uses the society's figure, attributed, plus 'nearly tripled in 1877', which the society and the Encyclopedia of Indianapolis both state. Kiefer's support: Lilly Archives says he solicited the other half-dozen local wholesalers; Wikipedia says two associated drugstores agreed to buy; the story says only that he asked other wholesalers to back Lilly. The Historical Society misplaces the manufacturing partnership in Paris, Illinois; the story follows the Lilly Archives (Johnston and Lilly in Indianapolis). Incorporation 1880 vs 1881: 'around 1880'.
notes: The main narrative source is the Lilly Archives' own biography (2008), hosted as a PDF on in.gov because lilly.com blocks automated requests. No first-person Lilly words on the 1876 decision were found, so the story quotes none. The slate's '$1,400' is confirmed as about $1,000 cash plus $400 in fluid extracts.
